title: The Landfall of the Empty Quarter
premise: August Nakamura, a digger who has spent years outrunning their famous mother's shadow and a warrant they never earned, is hired off the books to find a government survey team that vanished in the Empty Quarter's glacier fields, leaving equipment intact and no footprints. Following the team's route, August uncovers evidence that the expedition found a pre-colonial burial ground the government intends to strip-mine once the calving season opens the pass — and that the team didn't vanish, they were made to vanish. With the help of a disgraced surveyor and the team's lone survivor, August must move the evidence and the survivor out through the ice corridor before it seals, choosing at last to stop running and put their name on the record, whatever it costs. The book ends with the route closing behind them and August, publicly named and legally exposed, testifying as the glacier takes the site forever.
about_author: B. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping seasonal ice roads across the northern territories before turning to fiction. They write from a cabin that moves every few years, and refuse to confirm whether that is preference or habit.

chapters.title: Cash, No Questions
chapters.summary: August's POV. Working a black-market salvage dig in a border town, August is approached by a fixer offering triple rate to locate a missing government survey team — payment in cash, no paperwork, no names. August takes it because rent is due and running is expensive. Emotional beat: the weary competence of someone who has made impermanence an identity.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the abandoned survey camp, August finds tents pitched, food cached, radios functional — and not a single set of tracks leading out. The absence is deliberate, professional. A torn survey log hints the team found something they weren't supposed to map. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into the hunter's thrill August can't admit to enjoying.

chapters.title: The Surveyor Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, introducing Ilse Brandt, the survey team's cartographer, hiding in a trapper's cabin with frostbitten hands and a stolen data drive. She's been waiting for someone with August's skills to come down the route. Emotional beat: two people who survive by not being seen recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Ice Kept
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, with August listening. She describes the burial ground beneath the moraine — intact, ancient, and flagged for demolition in the government's mining schedule. The team voted to document it anyway; the next morning, an 'inspection' party arrived. Emotional beat: grief for colleagues and for a history about to be erased for ore.

chapters.title: Warrant, Unserved
chapters.summary: August's POV. The fixer's employer tracks August down: return Ilse and the drive, or the old warrant — the one pinned on August for a mother's crime — gets served. August learns the search was never about the team; it was about the drive. Emotional beat: the trap closing on the one person who thought they'd already paid.

chapters.title: The Calving Window
chapters.summary: August and Ilse's POV, alternating. They plan the run: the glacier route opens for eleven days when the ice shelf calves, then seals until next season. Eleven days to move Ilse, the drive, and August's own documentation out past the checkpoints. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership hardening into trust.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at the Moraine
chapters.summary: August's POV. The inspection party catches them mid-route. August buys Ilse's escape by surrendering a decoy drive and their own name — the first time in a decade they've said it aloud to an official. Emotional beat: the terror and strange relief of being visible.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Separated and storm-bound, Ilse must cross the crevasse field alone using August's route notes, carrying the real drive. She nearly dies at the ice bridge and survives by trusting a stranger's handwriting. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid forward by someone she's known four days.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. At the route's mouth, August confronts the fixer and the mining company's man, choosing arrest over the deal — buying time for Ilse's transmission of the survey to press and heritage bodies as the first calving cracks split the air. Emotional beat: the running stops; August stands still and lets the consequences land.

chapters.title: Named on the Record
chapters.summary: August's POV, weeks later. In a hearing room far from the ice, August testifies under their full name, the warrant dissolved, the site legally protected even as the calving season erases it. Ilse waits outside with coffee and no questions. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — identity chosen, not fled from.
